title: Synthesis and structural characterization of polynuclear divalent ytterbium complexes supported by a bis(phenolate) cyclam ligand

material_class.structural_family: trinuclear Yb(II) bis(phenolate) cyclam iodide cluster

synthesis.procedure: Under nitrogen, solid KH (40 mg, 1 mmol) was added to H2(Me2ArO)2Me2-cyclam (134 mg, 0.271 mmol) in thf (15 mL). After 16 h stirring at room temperature, the mixture was centrifuged. The resulting solution of 2-K was added to a yellow solution of [YbI2(thf)2.5] (247 mg, 0.406 mmol) in thf (10 mL), immediately turning strong orange. After stirring overnight at room temperature, KI was removed by centrifugation, the orange solution was concentrated and layered with n-hexane. An orange microcrystalline solid precipitated, was collected by centrifugation and dried under vacuum (103 mg, 0.058 mmol, 43%). Complex 4 crystallized from tetrahydrofuran as orange crystals with a discrete cationic trinuclear [Yb3] unit, one iodide and four lattice thf molecules.
synthesis.time: 16 h ligand deprotonation, then overnight metathesis
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: centrifuged to remove KI; concentrated thf solution layered with n-hexane; orange microcrystalline solid collected by centrifugation and dried under vacuum; crystals from thf

properties.summary: Air-sensitive orange Yb(II) solid; THF solutions show visible absorptions characteristic of divalent Yb, assigned to LMCT and spin-allowed f–d transitions rather than f–f transitions (closed-shell f14). An absorption near 453 nm (600 M−1 cm−1) is attributed to bis(phenolate) cyclam-to-ytterbium charge transfer and is absent for [YbI2(thf)2.5].

measurements.name: UV–Vis absorption (LMCT)
measurements.conditions: thf solution, room temperature; ε = 600 M−1 cm−1; related peaks between 471 and 290 nm

material_class.structural_family: dinuclear Yb(II) bis(phenolate) cyclam iodide–thf complex

synthesis.procedure: Under nitrogen, solid KH (79 mg, 1.98 mmol) was added to H2(Me2ArO)2Me2-cyclam (281 mg, 0.567 mmol) in thf (20 mL). After 16 h the mixture was centrifuged. The 2-K solution was added to [YbI2(thf)2.5] (689 mg, 1.135 mmol) in thf (15 mL), immediately turning strong orange-red. After stirring overnight at room temperature, KI was removed by centrifugation, the solution was concentrated and layered with n-hexane. An orange microcrystalline solid was collected by centrifugation and dried under vacuum (450 mg, 0.363 mmol, 64%). Orange-red crystals suitable for X-ray diffraction were grown from concentrated thf.
synthesis.time: 16 h ligand deprotonation, then overnight metathesis
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: centrifuged to remove KI; concentrated thf solution layered with n-hexane; orange solid dried under vacuum; X-ray crystals from concentrated thf

properties.summary: Air-sensitive orange-red Yb(II) dimer; THF solutions show visible absorptions characteristic of divalent Yb. An absorption near 467 nm (521 M−1 cm−1) is assigned to ligand-to-ytterbium charge transfer, with a maximum around 390 nm resembling [YbI2(thf)2.5].

measurements.name: UV–Vis absorption (LMCT)
measurements.conditions: thf solution, room temperature; ε = 521 M−1 cm−1; additional maximum around 390 nm
